t: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 was replaced by the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which was subsequently amended in:
o: 1990 and 1995 only
2005 and 2010 only
1989 only
e: The 1988 Act has been amended from time to time – 1994, 2000, 2001 and more recently 2019 (notified 09.08.2019) and 2022; the Central Motor Vehicles Rules were made in 1989.

t: Under the deleted Section 163A structured-formula provision, compensation for permanent disability was computed as:
o: ₹5,00,000 × percentage of disability per Schedule I of the Employees' Compensation Act, subject to a minimum of ₹50,000
A flat ₹2,50,000 for every disability
Loss of income × multiplier under the Second Schedule only
₹25,000 for every disability
e: Old s.163A (as amended in 2018) gave ₹5 lakh for death, ₹5 lakh × disability percentage (minimum ₹50,000) for permanent disability and ₹25,000 for minor injury; it was deleted in 2019.

t: Compensation paid to a victim out of the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund is:
o: In addition to the Tribunal award without adjustment
Recoverable from the victim if the Tribunal awards more
Deductible from any compensation the victim may later get from the Claims Tribunal
Payable only after the Tribunal award is passed
e: Under s.164B the compensation paid out of the Fund (interim relief, golden hour, hit and run) is deductible from the compensation the victim may receive from the Tribunal in future.

t: Under the pre-amendment Section 158(6), the officer-in-charge of the police station was to forward the accident report to the Claims Tribunal and insurer within:
o: Forty-eight hours of the accident
Thirty days of recording the information
Three months of the accident
Ten days of the FIR
e: Old s.158(6) prescribed thirty days; the new s.159 requires the police to prepare an accident information report within three months and submit it to the Tribunal and the prescribed agency.

t: A 'stage carriage' is a motor vehicle meant to carry:
o: More than six passengers excluding the driver, for hire or reward, at separate fares paid by individual passengers for the whole journey or stages of it
Specified passengers as a whole under a contract for a fixed sum
Goods along with passengers in the cabin
Up to six passengers for hire or reward on a single contract
e: A stage carriage serves the general public at separate fares; a contract carriage is hired collectively by a group for a fixed sum. A motor cab falls under the contract carriage category.

t: A 'motor car' under Section 2 of the MV Act is:
o: Any mechanically propelled vehicle including a trailer
A motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle, omnibus, road-roller, tractor, motorcycle or invalid carriage – a private passenger vehicle of up to 6+1 seats
Any four-wheeled vehicle used for hire or reward
A vehicle with seating capacity above 6+1
e: Motor car means a private-use passenger vehicle (seating up to 6+1) not used for hire or reward; a similar vehicle for hire is a motor cab.

t: An 'educational institution bus' is defined as:
o: A stage carriage plying on a route near a school
A private service vehicle owned by a parent-teacher association
Any contract carriage hired by a school occasionally
An omnibus for the exclusive use of transporting students and/or staff of an educational institution in connection with its activities
e: An educational institution bus is an omnibus used exclusively for students/staff of an educational institution; a private service vehicle carries persons for the owner's own trade/business, not for hire.

t: After the 2019 amendment, a non-transport licence issued to a person who has attained 55 years is valid for:
o: Till age 70
Till age 60
5 years
10 years
e: Age bands: below 30 – till 40; 30 to below 50 – 10 years; 50 to below 55 – till 60; 55 and above – 5 years.

t: Under the Good Samaritan provisions, hospitals are required to:
o: Detain the Good Samaritan till the police arrive
Display a charter in multiple languages detailing the rights of Good Samaritans
Report the Good Samaritan's details to the insurer
Recover treatment charges from the Good Samaritan
e: The rules under s.134A require hospitals to display a charter of Good Samaritan rights; a Good Samaritan cannot be compelled to disclose personal details or detained.

t: The compensation for death in a hit-and-run motor accident under the amended Section 161 is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2019 amendment raised hit-and-run compensation from ₹25,000 to ₹2,00,000 for death and from ₹12,500 to ₹50,000 for grievous hurt.

t: The Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme under Section 162 was notified by the Central Government on:
o: 1 April 2022
1 July 2024
1 September 2019
e: The Scheme was notified on 5 May 2025 (guidelines dated 4 June 2025), providing cashless treatment up to ₹1.5 lakh for seven days through designated hospitals.

t: A person who causes hurt to a pedestrian by rash driving (old Section 337 IPC) is now charged under:
o: Section 101 BNS
Section 106 BNS
Section 125(b) BNS
Section 125(a) BNS
e: Section 125(a) BNS covers hurt caused by an act endangering life or personal safety (old 337 IPC); 125(b) covers grievous hurt (old 338 IPC).

t: Magma General Insurance v. Nanu Ram (2018) is significant for:
o: Holding that an LMV licence covers transport vehicles up to 7,500 kg
Raising hit-and-run compensation to ₹2 lakh
Extending consortium to parental consortium (for children) and filial consortium (for parents) at the Pranay Sethi amounts
Introducing future prospects for self-employed persons
e: Pranay Sethi had dealt with spousal consortium; Magma v. Nanu Ram clarified that children (parental consortium) and parents (filial consortium) are also entitled, each at the fixed amount.

t: Bajaj Allianz v. Rambha Devi (2024) is a Constitution Bench decision that:
o: Abolished the pay-and-recover principle
Fixed the multiplier table for injury cases
Reaffirmed Mukund Dewangan – an LMV licence suffices for transport vehicles of GVW up to 7,500 kg without separate endorsement
Overruled Mukund Dewangan and mandated a transport endorsement for all commercial vehicles
e: Rambha Devi upheld Mukund Dewangan, confirming that no separate transport endorsement is needed for LMV-class transport vehicles.

t: The multiplier applicable for a deceased aged 36 to 40 years is:
As per the multiplier table approved in Pranay Sethi, the multiplier applicable where the deceased was aged 41 to 45 years is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The Sarla Verma table starts at 18 for ages 15–25 and reduces by one per five-year band: 17 (26–30), 16 (31–35), 15 (36–40), 14 (41–45), 13 (46–50), then 11, 9, 7 and 5.

t: For a self-employed deceased aged 35, the addition towards future prospects is:
e: Self-employed/fixed salary below 40 → 40%; permanent job below 40 → 50%.

t: In computing the multiplicand for a salaried deceased, Pranay Sethi requires the income to be taken as:
o: Gross salary including all allowances and perquisites
Actual salary less tax
Take-home pay after all loan deductions
Basic pay only
e: For permanent-job employees, actual salary less tax is the basis; for self-employed, established income less the tax component.

t: Per the trainers' limitation table, where the insurer makes an offer under Section 149 and it is accepted, payment must follow within:
o: 30 days of recording the settlement
15 days of acceptance
90 days of the offer
6 months of the accident
e: Offer within 30 days; payment within 30 days of the Tribunal recording the settlement; Tribunal's inquiry within 12 months where contested.

t: Under the amended Section 194D, riding a two-wheeler without a helmet attracts:
o: Fine of ₹1,000 and disqualification from holding a licence for three months
Fine of ₹100 only
Fine of ₹500 only
Fine of ₹5,000 and imprisonment up to 3 months
e: Section 194D (inserted 2019): fine of ₹1,000 and three months' disqualification. Not wearing a seat belt under s.194B attracts ₹1,000.

t: A two-wheeler rider with a valid licence collides with a car that jumped a red signal; the rider was speeding at 80 km/h in a 40 km/h zone. The Tribunal assesses the rider's share of blame at 30% and total loss at ₹10,00,000. The award is:
e: Contributory negligence of 30% reduces the compensation proportionately: 10,00,000 × 70% = ₹7,00,000.

topic: Third party – who is a third party
t: Which of the following IS a third party under an Act policy issued on a goods carriage?
o: A person who borrowed the vehicle and was driving it
The driver of the goods carriage injured in the accident (post-2019 amendment)
The registered owner travelling in the cabin
A gratuitous passenger sitting on the goods
e: The amended s.145 brings the driver and co-workers on a transport vehicle within 'third party'; gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle, the owner and the borrower are not third parties.

t: A goods carriage with permitted cabin seating of 1+2 carries six persons in the cabin, none of whom owns the goods. After an accident, under the Act policy:
o: None of the six is covered – they are gratuitous/unauthorised passengers in a goods vehicle
Only two of them are covered up to cabin capacity
They are covered under Section 164 for ₹5 lakh each
All six are covered as third parties
e: Gratuitous passengers in a goods carriage are specifically excluded under s.147; only the owner of goods or his authorised representative travelling with the goods is covered.

t: An insurer prefers to settle a weak-defence death claim at a Lok Adalat rather than contest it. The maximum amount the insurer should agree to is:
o: Any amount demanded by the claimant, since the award is unappealable
The compensation computed under Sarla Verma/Pranay Sethi without interest, as a Lok Adalat compromise is a full and final consent settlement
The hit-and-run amount of ₹2 lakh
The Section 164 fixed amount of ₹5 lakh only
e: The trainers' worked example treats the total computed under the judgements (e.g. ₹21,18,000) as the maximum allowable in a Lok Adalat compromise; interest and costs arise only on a contested award.

t: A Claims Tribunal awards ₹3,50,000. The insurer wishes to appeal. The minimum amount to be deposited for the appeal to be entertained is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 173 requires deposit of ₹25,000 or 50% of the award, whichever is less. 50% of 3,50,000 = 1,75,000, so ₹25,000 is deposited.

t: The insurer's designated officer receives the DAR showing clear negligence of its insured's driver and a deceased aged 40 with known income. The appropriate course under the scheme is:
o: Pay ₹5 lakh under Section 164 and close the file
Compute compensation under Pranay Sethi and submit Form XI accepting liability with an offer within 30 days
Wait for the Tribunal to pass an award after 12 months
File Form XI contesting liability to gain time
e: Where liability is clear, s.149 and the scheme expect the insurer to accept liability and make a fair offer in Form XI within 30 days of the DAR, enabling a consent award within six months.

t: A truck's insurance was obtained by misdeclaring it as a private carrier when it was a public carrier. In a TP claim, the insurer:
o: Has no defence because the vehicle was insured
May plead that the policy is void for misrepresentation of a material fact under Section 150(2)(b)
Can only plead non-receipt of premium
Must pay and has no recovery right
e: Section 150(2)(b) permits the insurer to avoid liability where the policy was obtained by non-disclosure or false representation of a material particular.

t: A fatal accident is caused by an insured bus during a riot in which the driver was forced to speed through a mob. The insurer can plead:
o: No defence at all
Use for hire without a permit
Driving by an unlicensed person
Breach of the policy condition excluding liability for injury caused or contributed to by riot or civil commotion
e: Section 150(2)(a)(iii) allows a condition excluding liability for injury caused or contributed to by war, civil war, riot or civil commotion to be pleaded.

t: Under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022, the claim application is enquired into and sanctioned respectively by:
o: The Claims Enquiry Officer and the Claims Settlement Commissioner (District Collector/Magistrate), with payment by GIC
The insurer's designated officer and IRDAI
The Claims Tribunal and the High Court
The police station and the State Transport Authority
e: The 2022 Scheme (effective 01.04.2022) provides for the Claims Enquiry Officer to enquire and report, the Claims Settlement Commissioner to sanction, and GIC as nodal agency to pay from the Hit and Run Compensation Fund.

t: A claimant, in the same petition, seeks ₹5 lakh under Section 164 and also ₹40 lakh under Section 166. The correct advice to the insurer's counsel is:
o: Pay both amounts, as they are independent statutory rights
Section 164 applies only to hit-and-run cases
The claimant must elect; s.164 is a fixed final payment and any amount paid under it is adjusted against a s.166 award for the same accident – both cannot be received cumulatively
Section 166 is barred once a s.164 claim is made
e: Section 164 compensation is full and final; compensation under any other law for the same accident is deducted. The claimant cannot aggregate both.

t: Before the 2019 amendment, a personal injury claim pending before the Tribunal would, on the claimant's death from an unrelated cause:
o: Automatically convert into a death claim
Survive to the legal heirs in all cases
Abate and not survive to the estate, by operation of Section 306 of the Indian Succession Act, unless death had nexus with the injuries
Be transferred to the Lok Adalat
e: Under the old law the claim survived only if death was connected with the injuries; the amendment now lets the right survive to legal representatives irrespective of nexus.

t: An insurer impleaded under Section 170 wishes to argue that the deceased's income is exaggerated and that the driver was not negligent. The insurer:
o: May contest only on quantum
Cannot contest at all once impleaded
May contest only on the statutory defences under Section 150(2)
May contest on all grounds available to the owner, including negligence and quantum
e: Once impleaded under s.170 (collusion or failure of the owner to contest), the insurer has the right to contest on all or any grounds available to the person against whom the claim is made.

t: A truck with GVW of 16,200 kg is found carrying a laden weight of 21,000 kg at the time of a fatal accident. Which provision has been contravened?
o: Section 128 – carrying excess persons
Section 157 – transfer of certificate
Section 129 – protective headgear
Section 113 – the laden weight must not exceed the GVW specified in the RC
e: Section 113 limits the laden weight to the GVW (and ULW as per RC); overloading is penalised under s.194 (₹20,000 plus ₹2,000 per excess tonne) and may be relevant to negligence.

t: Per Mukund Dewangan, 'gross vehicle weight' means:
o: The weight of the vehicle excluding the driver and attendant
The total weight of the vehicle and load certified and registered by the registering authority as permissible
The actual weight at the time of the accident
The weight of the heaviest alternative body only
e: GVW is the certified permissible total weight (vehicle plus load); ULW is the weight of the vehicle with equipment but excluding driver/attendant, taking the heaviest alternative body.

t: A car owner allows his unlicensed nephew to drive the car. Under the amended Act, the owner is liable under Section 180 to:
o: Fine of ₹1,000 only
Imprisonment up to 1 year only
Fine of ₹500 only
Imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine of ₹5,000
e: Section 180 (allowing an unauthorised person to drive): imprisonment up to three months and/or fine of ₹5,000 (earlier ₹1,000). Driving without licence under s.181 also attracts ₹5,000.

t: Under the amended Section 183, the fine for overspeeding a light motor vehicle is:
e: Section 183: LMV ₹1,000–2,000; medium/heavy vehicles ₹2,000–4,000. Dangerous driving under s.184 attracts ₹1,000–5,000 and/or imprisonment of six months to one year.

t: Under the detailed accident report scheme, within how many days must the Investigating Officer furnish the 'Rights of Victims of Road Accident' (Form II) to the victims?
o: 60 days
30 days
48 hours
10 days
e: Form II (rights of victims) within 10 days; victims respond with Forms VI-A and VI-B within 60 days.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
o: Sections 39 and 38
Sections 38 and 39
Sections 41 and 45
Sections 45 and 41
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Lok Adalat proceedings?
o: The settlement is by consent of parties
The proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings
The award is final and not appealable
The award carries interest at 7.5% from the date of petition as a matter of right
e: Interest under s.171 is a feature of contested Tribunal awards; Lok Adalat settlements are consent-based lump sums.

t: A 36-year-old self-employed contractor earning ₹35,000 per month dies in 2025 leaving wife and three children. Total compensation including conventional heads (+20%) is:
A 46-year-old permanent employee earning ₹45,000 per month dies leaving a wife and one child. Loss of dependency is:
A 67-year-old self-employed farmer earning ₹15,000 per month dies leaving only his wife. Loss of dependency is:

A 50-year-old salaried employee earning ₹40,000 per month suffers a 25% permanent disability which the Tribunal assesses as 25% loss of earning capacity. Compensation for loss of future earnings (ignoring future prospects) is:
e: 4,80,000 × 25% = 1,20,000 per annum × multiplier 13 (46–50) = ₹15,60,000; no deduction for personal expenses in injury claims.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
o: Insurance Act 1938
IRDA Act 1999
General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972
LIC Act 1956
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: A Tribunal awards ₹16,00,000 with 7.5% simple interest from the petition date; 292 days elapse till deposit. Interest payable (approx.) is:
Interest of ₹96,000 on an award is shared equally by two claimants, both with PAN. TDS is:
o: ₹4,800 from each
₹9,600 in total
₹19,200 in total
Nil, as each claimant's share of ₹48,000 does not exceed ₹50,000
e: TDS on MACT interest applies only where interest exceeds ₹50,000 per claimant; 48,000 each is below the threshold.

t: An accident occurs in 2020 (before October). The deceased leaves wife, two children and mother. Conventional heads under Pranay Sethi/Magma total:
e: No three-year span completed (Oct 2017–Oct 2020) → base amounts: consortium 40,000 × 4 = 1,60,000 + estate 15,000 + funeral 15,000 = ₹1,90,000.

t: An award of ₹2,00,000 is challenged by the insurer, which disputes ₹1,50,000 of it. The deposit required with the appeal is:
e: Deposit is the lesser of ₹25,000 and 50% of the amount awarded (₹1,00,000) → ₹25,000; the dispute exceeds ₹1 lakh so the appeal is maintainable.

t: A hit-and-run accident leaves two persons dead and one with a simple fracture-free injury. Total compensation payable under Section 161 is:
e: Death ₹2,00,000 × 2 = ₹4,00,000; simple (non-grievous) hurt attracts nothing under s.161.

t: A 28-year-old permanent employee earning ₹20,000 per month dies leaving wife, one child and both parents. Loss of dependency is:
